meta.name: Send monthly volunteer hour statements from Google Sheets with Gmail

name: Issue monthly volunteer hour statements from a Google Sheets ledger with Gmail

parameters.content:
# Volunteer Hour Statements and In-Kind Valuation

On the 1st of each month this workflow reads the verified volunteer hours ledger in Google Sheets, emails every volunteer a bank statement style summary of the previous calendar month, and sends the coordinator one program level summary with the total in-kind dollar value formatted for grant match reporting. A statements issued log Data Table makes re-runs safe: a period that has already been issued is never emailed twice.

## How it works
1. The Schedule Trigger fires monthly and the statement period is derived as the previous calendar month from the run date, never the last 30 days.
2. The statements issued log Data Table is checked first. If this period already has a log row the run stops.
3. Milestone thresholds, the in-kind hourly rate, and the zero hour policy are loaded from the Volunteer Statement Config Data Table.
4. A Code node groups ledger rows per volunteer: hours this period, year to date, progress to the next milestone, and dollar in-kind value.
5. Each volunteer receives an inline styled HTML statement through Gmail. One bad address does not stop the roster.
6. The coordinator receives the program summary and one log row is appended for the period.

## Setup
- Replace <__PLACEHOLDER_VALUE__VOLUNTEER_HOURS_SHEET_ID__> in Workflow Configuration with the ledger spreadsheet id.
- Replace <__PLACEHOLDER_VALUE__VOLUNTEER_HOURS_TAB_NAME__> with the tab holding columns: date, volunteer name, email, hours, activity.
- Replace <__PLACEHOLDER_VALUE__COORDINATOR_EMAIL__> with the coordinator inbox.
- Replace <__PLACEHOLDER_VALUE__ORG_NAME__> with your organization name.
- Open the Volunteer Statement Config Data Table and set in_kind_hourly_rate, milestone_thresholds, and include_zero_hour_volunteers.
- Connect Google Sheets and Gmail credentials, run once manually, then activate.

## 1. Trigger and period
Fires on the 1st of every month. Workflow Configuration centralizes every id, email, and name, and derives the statement period as the previous calendar month with Luxon: minus one month, then startOf and endOf month. This is a calendar month, never a rolling 30 days.

## 2. Idempotency gate
Before anything is sent, the issued log Data Table is checked for this period_key. If a row exists the run stops here, so a mid month manual re-run never re-emails the whole roster.

## 3. Load config and compute
Valuation settings live in the Volunteer Statement Config Data Table. The Code node groups ledger rows per volunteer: hours this period, year to date hours, progress toward the next milestone (25, 50, 100 by default), and the dollar in-kind value. The include_zero_hour_volunteers flag decides whether a volunteer with no hours this period but a year to date balance still receives a statement.

## 4. Send statements and log
Statements go out one volunteer at a time as inline styled HTML tables, because most email clients ignore style blocks. A failing address continues instead of killing the roster run. The coordinator summary totals the in-kind valuation for grant match reporting, then one row is appended to the issued log so this period cannot be sent twice.

nodes.name: Warning In Kind Rate Is Jurisdiction Dependent

parameters.content:
## In-kind rate is jurisdiction and year dependent
Do not hardcode a dollar figure in this workflow. US organizations usually cite the Independent Sector value of volunteer time, which is updated every year. Canada has no single official figure: organizations commonly use a provincial living wage or a role based replacement cost the funder accepts. Set the number in the in_kind_hourly_rate column of the Volunteer Statement Config Data Table and record its source in rate_note.
